OzyVTT · polish · consistency sweep 2

Second sweep

The parts the first sweep left out, captured from every page of the 23 approved mockups: section bars, phone headers, where each primary sits, tabs, toolbars, fields, tags, the top bar and the phone's tabs, segmented controls, cards and glass. 331 captures and 143 primaries. An amber frame and number mark a capture that differs from the rest of its pattern; the findings say how, and what would bring it in line.

What doesn't match

Eleven differences, most to least visible; the last is in the rules rather than the drawings. Tell me which fixes to make, by number.

1

Two primaries at once

The theme allows one primary in view (T rule 2). On 18 Codex and Compendium pages the section bar keeps its Cup (New, New homebrew) while the page shows its own (Start session 3, New quest, Log downtime, Publish, Make a homebrew copy); the Compendium's editor shows three (New homebrew, Done, Next: Ability scores). Prep handles the same case two other ways: an encounter steps New encounter down to a plain button, while Sound, Replays and the table screen's Prep drop the bar's search and New altogether.

Fix: the bar always keeps its search. When the page shows its own Cup, the bar's New steps down to a Base line button (+ New encounter, + New, + New homebrew), as Prep's encounter does, and New quest in its toolbar becomes a Base line button like New page. Where a page has two of its own, the step's or the open panel's action keeps the Cup and the title row's steps down (Done, Publish).

2

What a phone header names

Prep and a Codex page name their section in the header (PREP, CODEX) over the strip of pages, as T 2.1 says; the Atlas and the story name their page instead (ATLAS, STORY) over the same strip. A record names one of four things: the area (a Codex page, which also keeps the strip), its list with Back (an SRD monster: MONSTERS), its kind with Back and the strip (a homebrew record: MONSTER), or itself with Back (a screen: LIVING ROOM TV, with no title in its content). A's spec 2.2 and T's 2.2 also disagree on where a record's title goes.

Fix: a section's page names the section and its strip names the page. A record's header is Back and where it goes (PEOPLE, MONSTERS, TABLE SCREEN) with the record's own icons and no strip, and the title opens its content with its line, as T 2.2 says; A 2.2 is amended to match.

3

Strips a later round changed

Older mockups still draw strips that later rounds added to: the story's tabs without Downtime (the Codex, story and people, time and tools); Prep's pages as Encounters, Party and Maps in the table screen's menu; the table panel's tabs and the phone's switch without the bell, the counts and Token (the frame, the table). The Codex bar's More after New, which F's spec places (rule 8), is drawn only in Time and tools.

Fix: redraw each to its current set: Downtime in the story's tabs, Prep's seven pages, the panel's tabs as C3 draws them, and More after New in every Codex bar.

4

A list page with a title row

Replays opens with REPLAYS and 5 kept under the bar's lit Replays tab. A list has no title row (T 2.2), and a page never repeats its bar's choice (T rule 1).

Fix: drop the row; the count joins the list's toolbar as "5 replays".

5

A list's count and sort

Toolbars count three ways: "6 maps" (Prep, Maps, Tokens), "People · 4" (Pages), and in eyebrow capitals "ACTIVE · 2" and "ALL HOMEBREW · 4" (Quests, Sharing). Sort is the sort icon and its word (Modified), a caret and its word (Changed), or words inside the count (8 of 332 · by name).

Fix: the count first, in plain words ("4 people", "2 active quests", "4 homebrew records"); sort as the sort icon and its word (Changed, By name).

6

Fields

Maps' two choice fields (its type, its folder) put the caret before the value; every other choice field puts it at the right end. Four find fields draw their placeholder as bright as a typed value (Find a page by name, Find a quest, Filter pins, Find a path), and the API reference's has no search icon.

Fix: the caret at the right end; every find field with the search icon and a muted placeholder, as the section bars' searches are.

7

The Cup with an icon

Settings' New credential and the Compendium's New homebrew carry a + icon. Every other Cup is words only (New encounter, New character, Make live, Publish).

Fix: words only. A Base line New keeps its +.

8

Who sees a replay

A replay's row marks "players see it" with a magenta eye and "only you" with a muted struck eye. Its own spec says Only you is violet (F rule 2), magenta already means an Action, homebrew and the stat block, and the replay's own Players see it line is drawn the right way.

Fix: the eye in the dim text colour when players see it; violet and struck through when only you do.

9

A map's kind drawn as a state

A map's page shows Battle map as a boxed state tag, the look of Draft and Live. The Codex and the Compendium show a kind as its icon and word (Character, Monster).

Fix: the map icon and "Battle map", as a kind.

10

A player watching a replay

The top bar's menu button reads "Playing Lyra" beside her face, where A draws the face alone; and the phone lights Table, though a player's replays live under the Sheet (E3 2.5).

Fix: the face alone; Sheet lit.

11

Rule 13 asks too much of a side list's rows

Theme rule 13, written after the first sweep, says each side list row carries its icon. Every side list in fact gives an icon to rows that name a kind of thing (a folder, a kind, a map, a section, a person's face) and none to rows that filter (All maps, All pages, Active, Not started, Done, All sounds, Not on the board, each deadline). The drawings agree with each other; the rule doesn't describe them.

Fix: amend rule 13: a row that names a kind of thing carries its icon or face; a row that filters (All, a status, a view, a deadline) carries none.

Also checked, and matching: segmented controls, switches, group heads and their counts, cards, glass over maps, state tags and lamps, the phone's tabs and the top bar elsewhere. The first sweep's five parts, captured again, still read one way, apart from finding 11.
